questions.question: Which header requirements apply to 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP POST requests? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Mcp-Method is required on every request
Mcp-Name is required for tools/call, resources/read, and prompts/get
Servers reject requests where headers and body disagree (400 + HeaderMismatch, -32020)
Mcp-Session-Id is required for session affinity
x-mcp-header annotations can surface tool parameters as Mcp-Param-* headers

questions.explanation: Mcp-Session-Id was removed with protocol sessions. The rest is SEP-2243's header model, enabling gateways to route without parsing bodies.

questions.question: Which things were REMOVED from the Streamable HTTP transport in 2026-07-28? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Protocol-level sessions and the Mcp-Session-Id header
SSE stream resumability and message redelivery (Last-Event-ID, SSE event IDs)
The standalone HTTP GET endpoint for server-to-client notifications
The POST method for client messages
The initialize/notifications/initialized handshake

questions.explanation: Sessions, resumability, the GET notification endpoint (replaced by subscriptions/listen), and the handshake are gone. POST remains the way client messages travel.

questions.question: Which results must carry ttlMs and cacheScope under the CacheableResult requirement? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: tools/list
prompts/list
resources/list and resources/templates/list
resources/read
tools/call

questions.explanation: SEP-2549 requires the caching fields on the list endpoints and resources/read. Tool execution results are not cacheable list results.

questions.question: Which statements about progress and cancellation are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Progress requires the client to include a progressToken in the request's _meta
notifications/progress flows on the response stream of the request it relates to
Cancellation is a notification (notifications/cancelled) referencing the requestId, expecting no reply
A cancelled request still receives a normal final response
The subscriptions/listen stream carries progress notifications

questions.explanation: Progress rides the originating request's response stream (not subscriptions/listen), and a cancelled request produces no response — the server stops work and frees resources.

questions.question: Which _meta observability keys did SEP-414 standardize, and with what effect? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: traceparent
tracestate
baggage
A trace can follow one tool call from host through SDK, server, and downstream systems as a single span tree
A monotonically increasing request counter for rate limiting

questions.explanation: The three W3C Trace Context keys plus the resulting end-to-end correlation — everything listed is right.

questions.question: Which requests require the Mcp-Name header on Streamable HTTP? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: tools/call
resources/read
prompts/get
tools/list
All of the above

questions.explanation: Only the three that name a target carry Mcp-Name; list calls carry just Mcp-Method. 'All of the above' fails on D.

questions.question: How does subscriptions/listen behave? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: It is a single long-lived POST whose response stream carries the opted-in notifications
The client names the notification types it wants; the server acknowledges via notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged
The subscriptionId equals the listen request's JSON-RPC id and tags every notification
Delivery is guaranteed and replayed after reconnect
All of the above

questions.explanation: Delivery is best-effort — resumability was removed, so clients should still poll or refresh after a dropped stream. D poisons E.

questions.question: Which caching statements from SEP-2549 are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: ttlMs is a freshness hint in milliseconds
cacheScope: "public" permits shared intermediaries to cache; "private" restricts caching to the client
A list_changed notification supersedes an unexpired TTL
The fields appear on tools/list, prompts/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, and resources/read results
TTL values must be set by the server and cannot be overridden by the client

questions.explanation: All four describe the CacheableResult contract accurately.
